title: Content
description: A single piece of marketing content (e.g. a post, a caption, an article draft) produced for Rough Draft Builders Club (RDBC). This is a schema *contract* only (architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §8); no runtime enforces it yet (src/ does not exist before Phase 16) — Phase 13 ("Content Production") produces real instances against this shape. `PUBLISHED` is a structurally-defined value of `status` that this project cannot currently reach: PUBLISHING_POLICY.md currently resolves all publishing to `DENY` (policy/action_registry.json ACT-P01, ACT-P04, ACT-P05), and no capability may skip a stage of the D-010 maturity ladder (every production-facing capability is DISABLED as of this writing, CLAUDE.md §13). This schema defines the shape a published-content record would have; it grants no permission to reach that state. `approval_id` links this record to the approval workflow (APPROVAL_POLICY.md §2; architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §6) rather than embedding approval states inside this schema's own `status` enum. See architecture/STATE_MACHINE.md for this entity's documented lifecycle transitions between `status` values.

id.description: Server-assigned identity. Never client-supplied, never reused. Shared envelope field, architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §2.1.

schema_version.description: The exact semver version of content.schema.json this record was written against. architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §2.1, §3.

idempotency_key.description: Caller-chosen deduplication key; a create request whose idempotency_key matches an existing content record returns the existing record rather than creating a duplicate. architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §2.1, §4.

status.description: This content item's own production/publishing lifecycle status — distinct from the linked approval record's status (`approval_id` below; see architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §6, which requires these to stay two separate, linked concepts rather than one merged enum). Enum values and reasoning are this schema's own design choice (Data Architect, Phase 04); transitions between them are documented separately in architecture/STATE_MACHINE.md, which cites this exact enum. DRAFT: the content is being authored and has not been submitted for review. READY_FOR_REVIEW: authoring is complete and the content is ready for an approval request to be submitted against it, per APPROVAL_POLICY.md §4. SCHEDULED: the content has been approved and queued for a future publish action — structurally defined even though no scheduling capability is authorized today (ACT-P04 is DENY). PUBLISHED: the content has been published to its intended audience. As stated in this schema's top-level description, this value cannot currently be reached by any lawful path in this project — it is defined for shape completeness, not as a reachable state today. ARCHIVED: the content is no longer active (whether it was ever published or not) and is retained for record-keeping only.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 / RFC 3339. Set once, never mutated. architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §2.1.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 / RFC 3339. Set on every accepted mutation; must be >= created_at. architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §2.1.

created_by_role.description: Which role created this record — a closed role token from policy/action_registry.json's `roles` array, never a person's name or an invented role. architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §2.1.

title.description: A short structural label identifying this content item internally (e.g. for a queue or index) — not itself the published copy.

body.description: The content's own text/copy. Any claim, testimonial, price, discount, or controversial-topic statement this text contains falls under the corresponding gated category (CLAUDE.md §4) the moment publication is attempted — storing text here is authoring inside the gates (ACT-P02, ALLOW), never itself a publish action (ACT-P01, DENY).

approval_id.description: References the approval record (APPROVAL_POLICY.md §2; schemas/approval.schema.json) governing this content item, if any request has been submitted. Null until an approval request exists for this artifact. Per architecture/DATA_CONTRACTS.md §6, this content record composes with at most one active approval record by reference — it never embeds the approval workflow's own states inside this schema's `status` enum above.
